abstract.reader_question: How can exact attention run faster without approximating its output?
abstract.expected_relation: Reducing non-matrix work and reorganizing GPU work assignment improves hardware use while preserving the attention computation.

abstract.reader_question: Which performance level and workloads support the acceleration claim?
abstract.expected_relation: Attention-kernel timing and full-model training throughput describe different scopes; gains depend on the measured shapes, masks and hardware.

methods.reader_question: How do scheduling choices connect to the attention bottlenecks?
methods.expected_relation: Sequence-level blocks improve occupancy, while independently assigned warp outputs reduce communication; decoding instead emphasizes parallel cache loading.

methods.reader_question: What makes the different benchmark comparisons interpretable?
methods.expected_relation: Training kernels, multi-query decoding and multi-GPU training have distinct workload controls and timing or FLOP conventions that constrain comparison.

results.reader_question: How do kernel measurements relate to full-model performance?
results.expected_relation: Kernel efficiency and end-to-end throughput are related but need not improve by the same factor; the complete workload matrix connects the two measurements.

results.reader_question: What limits interpretation of the reported throughput?
results.expected_relation: Unavailable baseline runs, FLOP-count conventions and unexploited H100 features bound the evidence rather than establishing universal hardware or workload gains.
